extra.message: User-controlled 'host' query parameter is concatenated directly into an os.system() shell command. An attacker can inject arbitrary shell commands (e.g., host='127.0.0.1; cat /etc/passwd') to achieve Remote Code Execution.

User-controlled 'fragment' query parameter is concatenated directly into a Jinja2 Template string. An attacker can inject Jinja2 expressions (e.g., fragment='{{ config.__class__.__init__.__globals__ }}') to achieve Server-Side Template Injection (SSTI) and potentially Remote Code Execution.

User-supplied JSON from the request body is used directly as a MongoDB query filter via find_one(query). An attacker can inject MongoDB operators (e.g., {'$gt': ''}, {'$ne': ''}, {'$regex': '.*'}) to bypass authentication, extract arbitrary data, or manipulate the NoSQL query.

The SPA fallback route accepts a user-controlled 'path' parameter and constructs a file path via 'frontend_dist / path' without sanitization. An attacker can use path traversal (../../../etc/passwd) to read arbitrary files from the server filesystem. FastAPI URL-decodes the path, and Pathlib's / operator does not resolve '..' components — the OS kernel resolves them at the filesystem level when exists()/is_file()/FileResponse access the file.

User-controlled 'name' query parameter is used directly in 'BASE_EXPORT_DIR / name' to construct a file path for writing binary data. An attacker can use path traversal (e.g., name='../../evil.sh') to write arbitrary files anywhere on the filesystem that the app can access.

User-controlled 'ref' query parameter (or JSON payload key) is used directly in 'BASE_EXPORT_DIR / f"{ref}.json"' to construct a file path for writing JSON data. An attacker can use path traversal (e.g., ref='../../malicious') to write arbitrary JSON files anywhere on the filesystem.

User-controlled 'copyline' query parameter is concatenated directly into an HTML string with no escaping or sanitization, then returned as HTMLResponse. An attacker can inject arbitrary HTML/JavaScript (e.g., copyline='<script>alert(1)</script>') for stored or reflected XSS.

User-controlled 'card' query parameter is rendered with the '|safe' Jinja2 filter, which explicitly disables auto-escaping. An attacker can inject arbitrary HTML/JavaScript (e.g., card='') for reflected XSS.

User-controlled 'lane' query parameter is passed directly to RedirectResponse without any validation. An attacker can redirect users to arbitrary external domains (e.g., lane='https://evil.com') for phishing attacks.

Request body content and the Authorization header value are logged at WARNING level via logger.warning(). This can expose sensitive credentials (Bearer tokens, passwords, API keys) in log files which may be accessible to unauthorized parties.

extra.message: The endpoint mirrors the request's Origin header into the Access-Control-Allow-Origin response header while also setting Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true. Any requesting origin can trigger authenticated CORS requests, enabling cross-origin attacks that steal user credentials or session data.

This exposes sensitive operational and personal data.

extra.message: Endpoint explicitly disables XSS protection (X-XSS-Protection: 0) and clears Content-Security-Policy (CSP: empty string), removing browser-based security controls and making the application vulnerable to XSS and other client-side attacks.

The endpoint accepts arbitrary JSON from the request body and merges it into a workset dictionary with .update(change_set). An attacker can override critical fields like 'is_admin', 'role', or 'credit_limit', gaining unauthorized privileges.

Endpoint checks access based on a raw cookie value ('ops_badge') or header ('x-ops-badge') using a simple string comparison (if badge == 'lead'). No cryptographic verification or session validation is performed, allowing anyone who sets the cookie/header to 'lead' to gain elevated access.

Hardcoded demo password ('DemoPass!2026') and API key ('sd_demo_api_key_2026') are embedded in the seed source code. These credentials are used to create real user accounts and API keys, and if exposed through source code leaks, allow unauthorized access to the application.

User-controlled 'length' parameter has no upper bound, allowing an attacker to request extremely long strings (e.g., length=100000000) that consume excessive CPU and memory, causing Denial of Service.

cwe: CWE-770: Allocation of Resources Without Limits or Throttling

extra.message: Endpoint accepts arbitrary binary data via request.body() and writes it to disk without any size limit. An attacker can upload extremely large payloads to exhaust disk space and cause Denial of Service.
